overview.headline: Deep time from Steno laws and uniformitarianism to radiometric dating with half life

keyPoints.point: law of superposition shows older rocks on bottom and younger rocks on top revealing relative time
keyPoints.quote: The law of superposition says that older rocks are on the bottom and younger rocks are on the top.

keyPoints.point: James Hutton proposed foundational principle of geology called uniformitarianism in 1788
keyPoints.quote: In 1788, James Hutton proposed what would become the foundational principle of geology — uniformitarianism.

keyPoints.point: Lord Kelvin cooling magma calculations yielded age of 20 to 400 million years for Earth
keyPoints.quote: Lord Kelvin’s cooling-magma calculations yielded an age of 20–400 million years.

keyPoints.point: Clair Cameron Patterson used lead lead dating in 1956 to determine Canyon Diablo meteorite was 4.55 billion years old
keyPoints.quote: Clair Cameron Patterson, an American geochemist, used lead-lead dating to determine that the Canyon Diablo meteorite was 4.55 billion years old.

keyTerms.gloss: rule that older rocks sit below younger rocks indicating relative age order
keyTerms.quote: The law of superposition says that older rocks are on the bottom and younger rocks are on the top.

keyTerms.gloss: foundational principle that same geologic processes acting today shaped Earth in the past
keyTerms.quote: In 1788, James Hutton proposed what would become the foundational principle of geology — uniformitarianism.

keyTerms.gloss: law that species become extinct and are replaced by new species in characteristic fossil order
keyTerms.quote: In 1815, Smith developed the law of faunal succession, which states that species become extinct and are replaced by new species

keyTerms.gloss: gaps in geologic record representing missing time where strata were eroded
keyTerms.quote: He also understood the concept of unconformities (gaps in the geologic record that represent missing time)

keyTerms.gloss: time required for half of parent isotopes to decay to daughter isotope
keyTerms.quote: A half-life is the length of time it takes for half of the number of original, or parent, isotopes to decay to a stable daughter isotope.

keyTerms.gloss: technique using radioactive decay to assign numeric ages to rocks and meteorites
keyTerms.quote: radiometric dating. The next forty years would be pivotal. Chemists and physicists discovered hundreds of radioactive isotopes
